$comment: Which languages a model is good at, and whether anybody checked. Bean `46uh`, on the owner's instruction: 'should clarify each new model added to bootstrap which of the preferred languages ... especially if human validated'. EMPTY ON PURPOSE, and the emptiness is reported rather than silent — `check:model-languages` names it as a finding at every run. Two reasons it ships empty. First, an agent is not a valid source: a model's own claim about which languages it handles well is a generated assertion about a generated system, which is the exact thing `validation` exists to distrust, so an agent populating this would be manufacturing the evidence the schema asks for. Only `human-validated` is ever acted on, and only a person can grant it. Second, a language claim about a model is a claim about a third party's system, and writing one nobody checked would be worse than the fallback it replaces. Add an entry when a person has actually looked: id, title, preferredLanguages (an EMPTY list is a determined empty — somebody looked and found none notable; `validation: "unverified"` is nobody having looked), validation, and validatedBy + validatedOn when human-validated. Schema: schemas/model-registry.ts. How the languages are USED — as one input, never the answer: skills/communication-language.md.
